title: Generate contracts for dynamically named API documents
goal: Discover all OpenAPI document names offered by an application when names come from configuration, and generate matching runtime and build-time contracts.

selectionNotes: Use AddOpenApiCore() with IAdditionalOpenApiDocumentNameResolver and separately configured named OpenApiOptions. The built-in provider enumerates explicit plus additional names; strings alone do not configure documents. No .NET 10 backport or universal provider contract is claimed.

packageAssets: Current OpenApi 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105 selects lib/net11.0; previous OpenApi 10.0.13 selects lib/net10.0. Microsoft.OpenApi 3.10.2 and 2.12.2 respectively both select lib/net8.0. ApiDescription.Server contributes build props/targets and GetDocument tools, not a runtime library: current 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105, previous 10.0.0. Separate locked graphs, selected assets and ZIP hashes are retained. The audit's metadata-only previous ApiDescription.Server 10.0.13 is not asserted byte-identical to the executed 10.0.0 baseline.
providers: Built-in ASP.NET Core OpenAPI document provider, ApiDescription.Server GetDocument, Kestrel and System.Text.Json. No database/cloud provider.
platforms: ASP.NET Core supported server platforms; actual managed execution on Windows x64.
renderingModes: Server HTTP JSON documents; no browser or Blazor rendering mode.
prerequisites: Restore pinned packages and framework packs before execution. The installed Playbook guidance itself is complete offline and needs no account/key.
Use the canonical separate SDK pins for the older/newer examples. These verification pins are distinct from consumer release-family requirements.
constraints: Use AddOpenApiCore() with IAdditionalOpenApiDocumentNameResolver and separately configured named OpenApiOptions. The built-in provider enumerates explicit plus additional names; strings alone do not configure documents. No .NET 10 backport or universal provider contract is claimed.

Build-time generation executes startup with the tool mock server. Keep route/options/transformer registration intact and avoid production resource side effects. Use stable lowercase nonempty safe names; validate application configuration before exposing names.

Document grouping controls description membership, not endpoint authorization. The fictional staff endpoint is intentionally callable for the bounded local checks. Secure staff endpoints and document access separately in a deployed service.

No claim of trimming, AOT, generated client/parser support, hot reload of document sets, arbitrary names, other providers or OS-specific execution. .NET 10 is a valid explicit-registration comparison, not a supported target for the new APIs.
stabilityLimitations: Nonexperimental public API in the pinned .NET 11 RC2 artifact; no opt-in or warning suppression. Actual GA reconciliation and PIN-959 comprehensive readiness remain open.
